answer: SilverBullet Desktop's MCP endpoint defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:3999/.mcp`, a loopback listener. It's off by default. You can turn it on or change the port under **Settings → Advanced → MCP**. This is from `MCP.md`.

MCP.md:7:SilverBullet can act as an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (Model Context Protocol) server, so AI assistants can read, write, query and pimp up your spaces.
MCP.md:9:MCP is available in [[Dashboard|multi-space mode]] and in [[Desktop]]. The endpoint is `/.mcp` on your server, for example `https://notes.example.com/.mcp`. A single-space server does not serve it. On a server it is off by default: an admin turns it on in the APIs tab of the [[Dashboard]].
MCP.md:31:codex mcp add silverbullet --url https://notes.example.com/.mcp
MCP.md:32:codex mcp login silverbullet
MCP.md:37:claude mcp add --transport http silverbullet https://notes.example.com/.mcp
MCP.md:40:Then run `/mcp` inside Claude Code and choose to sign in.
MCP.md:43:Add a custom connector (Claude.ai: Settings, Connectors; ChatGPT: Settings, Connectors, developer mode) with the URL `https://notes.example.com/.mcp` and sign in when asked.
MCP.md:46:Any client that speaks Streamable HTTP MCP and supports OAuth 2.1 should work. A client identifies itself with a client ID metadata document (an https URL as its client ID) or registers dynamically. Most clients are public and rely on PKCE alone; a client whose metadata document registers `private_key_jwt` (as ChatGPT does) must also sign a client assertion at the token endpoint with a key from its published JWKS (RS256, PS256 or ES256).
MCP.md:49:SilverBullet Desktop serves MCP too, for the spaces registered in the app, on a loopback listener at `http://127.0.0.1:3999/.mcp`. It is off by default. Turn it on or change the port under **Settings → Advanced → MCP**, which also shows the setup commands with your port filled in.
